title: Meditation and wisdom are one
hookLine: Huineng: like a lamp and its light, meditation and wisdom are one

cards: Which comes first, the lamp or its light? It sounds like a riddle for children, and then it doesn't. Strike a match and touch it to a wick.
Is there a moment when the flame is burning but not yet giving light? When the light is shining with no flame behind it? Try to find the seam.
There isn't one. Huineng reached for exactly this picture to show how two parts of practice fit together, the quiet part and the seeing part.

teach.b: In the Platform Sutra, Huineng tells his listeners that his teaching rests on two things, often translated meditation and wisdom. Meditation here means the steadiness of a settled mind. Wisdom means clear seeing.
It's natural to treat them as a sequence: first I'll get calm, and once I'm calm enough, insight will come. Huineng says, in paraphrase, don't be confused into thinking they are different.

teach.h: NOT FIRST ONE, THEN THE OTHER.
teach.b: People who say meditation first and then wisdom, or wisdom first and then meditation, have already split them in two. Then the lamp. In paraphrase again: meditation and wisdom are like a lamp and its light.
Where there is a lamp, there is light. Where there is no lamp, there is darkness.

The lamp is the body of the light, and the light is what the lamp does. They have two names, he says, but one substance. If they're one, then steadiness is not a waiting room you sit in until wisdom shows up.
A steady moment is already a seeing moment. When you pause before answering an angry text, the pause isn't just calm. It's also where you see what the text actually says.
Huineng's word for the relationship is body and function, and it fits with his no-thought: the mind doesn't go blank to become wise.
Its stillness is already giving light.

how: Zen and Chan teachers often cite Huineng's lamp and light when they explain that sitting is not only a way to calm down before insight, but already a form of clear seeing.

games.q: what does “meditation and wisdom are one” mean?
o: wisdom matters, so meditation can be skipped
a lamp lit to mark the end of a retreat
steadiness and clear seeing arrive together

games.q: meditation and wisdom: tap the pairs.

s: Huineng teaches meditation first, and wisdom afterward
he says that putting either one first has already split them in two.
Huineng calls meditation the body of wisdom, and wisdom its function
like a lamp and the light it gives.
in his image, the lamp and its light are two separate things
two names, he says, but one substance.

games.q: a student tells Huineng: first I'll get calm, then I'll get wise. what does he answer?
o: good plan: one step at a time
that splits them; they're one, like a lamp and its light
skip the calm; wisdom is all that matters
games.why: Huineng warns against putting either first. where there's a lamp there's light; steadiness and seeing come together.

practice: If you have a candle or a small lamp nearby, and it's safe to, light it and set it in front of you; if not, any light will do, a window or a screen dimmed low.
Rest your eyes on it, watch steadily, and see whether, while you're watching steadily, you're also seeing clearly. Look for the seam between the steadiness and the seeing.

wordCard.voice: Meditation and wisdom are one. Huineng's teaching in the Platform Sutra: two names, one substance, like a lamp and its light. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese (ding hui): meditation and wisdom, the pair Huineng says are one, like a lamp and its light.

carryVoice: Your line: the lamp and its light. Steady and seeing, in the same moment. Tomorrow, an ox goes missing.

sources.ref: Platform Sutra, the teaching on meditation and wisdom (the lamp and its light)
sources.work: The Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch
